projects/keychron-c100/guides/keychron-c.title: Keychron C100 Unicode Firmware Guide
projects/keychron-c100/guides/keychron-c.content:
Complete rebuild / recovery notes
Original build date: 2026-09-16
Keyboard: Keychron C100 8K, 10×10 physical key grid
Host used: Windows 11 + WSL2 / Ubuntu
Firmware base: Keychron’s QMK fork, 2025q3 branch
QMK target: keychron/c100_8k
Flash interface: AT32 DFU, VID:PID 2e3c:df11
Flash tool that actually worked: dfu-util inside WSL, with the DFU USB device passed through by usbipd-win


                  
                  IMPORTANT
                  
                

This is custom keyboard firmware, not a Windows keyboard driver.
The only Windows driver work in this process is giving the C100’s DFU bootloader
a WinUSB driver so WSL / dfu-util can talk to it.


This note is deliberately self-contained. The goal is that Future Me can rebuild the entire thing even if the old working directory, ZIP file, or ChatGPT conversation is gone.

1. What the finished keyboard does
Every one of the C100’s 100 physical keys sends a unique Unicode symbol.
© ® ™ ℠ ℗ § ¶ № † ‡
¢ £ € ¥ ₹ ₩ ₽ ₺ ₴ ₿
± × ÷ ≠ ≈ ≤ ≥ ∞ √ ∫
∑ ∏ ∂ ∆ π µ Ω λ α β
° ‰ ¹ ² ³ ⁰ ½ ¼ ¾ ⌀
… • · – — ‐ “ ” ‘ ’
← ↑ → ↓ ↔ ↕ ↖ ↗ ↘ ↙
⇐ ⇒ ⇑ ⇓ ↩ ↪ ↺ ↻ ⤴ ⤵
✓ ✔ ✕ ✖ ☑ ☐ ☒ ★ ☆ ※
♠ ♥ ♦ ♣ ♪ ♫ ☺ ☹ ♂ ♀
There are no macro slots involved. QMK’s Unicode support is compiled directly into the firmware.
The full keymap uses calls such as:
UC(0x00A9) // ©
UC(0x2122) // ™
UC(0x2192) // →
UC(0x2605) // ★

2. The DFU / recovery method — do not change this
The normal, tested recovery method is:

Unplug the C100.
Hold the physical top-left key.
Plug the USB cable back in while continuing to hold that key.
Release it after a couple of seconds.
The C100 enters its AT32 DFU bootloader.

When it is in DFU mode, the normal keyboard lighting may remain off. That is fine.
The DFU device appears as:
DFU in FS Mode
VID:PID 2E3C:DF11
In WSL, lsusb showed:
2e3c:df11 Artery-Tech DFU in FS Mode
This top-left-key bootloader method was tested after custom firmware was already installed, so it is not dependent on the 100-key application keymap.
Do not sacrifice a normal key for DFU. Do not add a DFU combo. The hardware/startup method already works.

3. Windows Unicode prerequisite
QMK’s Windows Unicode mode uses Windows’ HexNumpad input mechanism.
Open Command Prompt or PowerShell on Windows and run:
reg add "HKCU\Control Panel\Input Method" /v EnableHexNumpad /t REG_SZ /d 1 /f
Then sign out and back in, or reboot Windows.
This only needs to be done once per Windows installation/user profile.

4. Install / prepare WSL2
Install Ubuntu under WSL2 if it is not already available.
Open the Ubuntu / WSL terminal and create a working directory:
mkdir -p ~/c100-dev
cd ~/c100-dev
Install QMK’s setup tooling:
curl -fsSL install.qmk.fm | sh
On the machine used for the original build, the ARM compiler was still missing afterward, so explicitly install the pieces we actually needed:
sudo apt update
sudo apt install gcc-arm-none-eabi binutils-arm-none-eabi libnewlib-arm-none-eabi
Verify:
arm-none-eabi-gcc --version
Also install dfu-util:
sudo apt install dfu-util
That package also supplied the dfu-suffix utility required near the end of the QMK build.
Optional, if needed for moving ZIPs around:
sudo apt install unzip

5. Clone Keychron’s QMK fork
From:
cd ~/c100-dev
clone the Keychron repository and the branch that contained the working C100 8K target:
git clone --branch 2025q3 --recurse-submodules \
  github.com/Keychron/qmk_firmware.git
The final directory should be:
~/c100-dev/qmk_firmware

6. Create the custom userspace project
Create this directory tree beside qmk_firmware:
~/c100-dev/
├── qmk_firmware/
└── c100-symbol-pad/
    ├── Makefile
    └── keyboards/
        └── keychron/
            └── c100_8k/
                └── keymaps/
                    ├── unicode_test/
                    │   ├── config.h
                    │   ├── keymap.c
                    │   └── rules.mk
                    └── symbol_pad/
                        ├── config.h
                        ├── keymap.c
                        └── rules.mk
Create it with:
cd ~/c100-dev
mkdir -p c100-symbol-pad/keyboards/keychron/c100_8k/keymaps/unicode_test
mkdir -p c100-symbol-pad/keyboards/keychron/c100_8k/keymaps/symbol_pad
cd c100-symbol-pad

7. Project Makefile
Create:
~/c100-dev/c100-symbol-pad/Makefile
with:
QMK_HOME ?= ../qmk_firmware
USERSPACE_PATH ?= $(CURDIR)
 
.PHONY: test full clean
 
define run_qmk
	@set -eu; \
	tmp=$$(mktemp -d); \
	ln -s "$(USERSPACE_PATH)" "$$tmp/userspace"; \
	trap 'rm -f "$$tmp/userspace"; rmdir "$$tmp"' EXIT; \
	$(MAKE) -C "$(QMK_HOME)" keychron/c100_8k:$(1) QMK_USERSPACE="$$tmp/userspace"
endef
 
test:
	$(call run_qmk,unicode_test)
 
full:
	$(call run_qmk,symbol_pad)
 
clean:
	$(MAKE) -C "$(QMK_HOME)" clean
 
This is the little wrapper that allowed the custom keymaps to live outside the cloned QMK repository while still being discovered as QMK userspace.

8. Shared QMK configuration
Both unicode_test and symbol_pad use the same config.h and rules.mk.
config.h
Put this in both:
keyboards/keychron/c100_8k/keymaps/unicode_test/config.h
keyboards/keychron/c100_8k/keymaps/symbol_pad/config.h
#pragma once
 
// Windows-only build. QMK emits Windows HexNumpad Unicode sequences.
#define UNICODE_SELECTED_MODES UNICODE_MODE_WINDOWS
#define UNICODE_CYCLE_PERSIST false
 
rules.mk
Put this in both:
keyboards/keychron/c100_8k/keymaps/unicode_test/rules.mk
keyboards/keychron/c100_8k/keymaps/symbol_pad/rules.mk
UNICODE_COMMON = yes
UNICODE_ENABLE = yes
VIA_ENABLE = no
 
# Keychron's C100 source produced an unused-variable warning in an RGB effect
# during this build. Do not promote that warning to a build-stopping error.
CFLAGS += -Wno-error=unused-but-set-variable
 
VIA_ENABLE = no is intentional for this dedicated symbol-pad firmware. Keychron Launcher / VIA functionality is not part of this build.

9. Build a safe one-key test first
Do not make the first ever flash the 100-key version.
Create:
keyboards/keychron/c100_8k/keymaps/unicode_test/keymap.c
with:
#include QMK_KEYBOARD_H
 
void keyboard_post_init_user(void) {
    set_unicode_input_mode(UNICODE_MODE_WINDOWS);
}
 
// Proof-of-concept:
// - top-left key: ©
// - top-right key: QK_BOOT
// - every other key: disabled
//
// IMPORTANT:
// The C100's normal hardware DFU entry still works independently:
// unplug, hold the PHYSICAL top-left key, reconnect USB.
const uint16_t PROGMEM keymaps[][MATRIX_ROWS][MATRIX_COLS] = {
    [0] = LAYOUT_tkl_ansi(
        UC(0x00A9), KC_NO, KC_NO, KC_NO, KC_NO, KC_NO, KC_NO, KC_NO, KC_NO, QK_BOOT,
        KC_NO, KC_NO, KC_NO, KC_NO, KC_NO, KC_NO, KC_NO, KC_NO, KC_NO, KC_NO,
        KC_NO, KC_NO, KC_NO, KC_NO, KC_NO, KC_NO, KC_NO, KC_NO, KC_NO, KC_NO,
        KC_NO, KC_NO, KC_NO, KC_NO, KC_NO, KC_NO, KC_NO, KC_NO, KC_NO, KC_NO,
        KC_NO, KC_NO, KC_NO, KC_NO, KC_NO, KC_NO, KC_NO, KC_NO, KC_NO, KC_NO,
        KC_NO, KC_NO, KC_NO, KC_NO, KC_NO, KC_NO, KC_NO, KC_NO, KC_NO, KC_NO,
        KC_NO, KC_NO, KC_NO, KC_NO, KC_NO, KC_NO, KC_NO, KC_NO, KC_NO, KC_NO,
        KC_NO, KC_NO, KC_NO, KC_NO, KC_NO, KC_NO, KC_NO, KC_NO, KC_NO, KC_NO,
        KC_NO, KC_NO, KC_NO, KC_NO, KC_NO, KC_NO, KC_NO, KC_NO, KC_NO, KC_NO,
        KC_NO, KC_NO, KC_NO, KC_NO, KC_NO, KC_NO, KC_NO, KC_NO, KC_NO, KC_NO
    )
};
 
This firmware intentionally makes:

physical top-left → ©
physical top-right → QK_BOOT
other 98 keys → disabled

The QK_BOOT mapping is only a convenience in the test firmware. It is not needed for recovery and is not present in the final 100-symbol firmware.
Build it:
cd ~/c100-dev/c100-symbol-pad
make test QMK_HOME=../qmk_firmware
A successful build ends with lines similar to:
Creating binary load file for flashing: .build/keychron_c100_8k_unicode_test.bin [OK]
Creating load file for flashing: .build/keychron_c100_8k_unicode_test.hex [OK]
The binary is:
~/c100-dev/qmk_firmware/.build/keychron_c100_8k_unicode_test.bin

10. Full 100-key keymap.c
Create:
keyboards/keychron/c100_8k/keymaps/symbol_pad/keymap.c
with:
#include QMK_KEYBOARD_H
 
void keyboard_post_init_user(void) {
    set_unicode_input_mode(UNICODE_MODE_WINDOWS);
}
 
// 10x10 symbol pad. Physical order is top-left to bottom-right.
const uint16_t PROGMEM keymaps[][MATRIX_ROWS][MATRIX_COLS] = {
    [0] = LAYOUT_tkl_ansi(
        UC(0x00A9), UC(0x00AE), UC(0x2122), UC(0x2120), UC(0x2117), UC(0x00A7), UC(0x00B6), UC(0x2116), UC(0x2020), UC(0x2021),
        UC(0x00A2), UC(0x00A3), UC(0x20AC), UC(0x00A5), UC(0x20B9), UC(0x20A9), UC(0x20BD), UC(0x20BA), UC(0x20B4), UC(0x20BF),
        UC(0x00B1), UC(0x00D7), UC(0x00F7), UC(0x2260), UC(0x2248), UC(0x2264), UC(0x2265), UC(0x221E), UC(0x221A), UC(0x222B),
        UC(0x2211), UC(0x220F), UC(0x2202), UC(0x2206), UC(0x03C0), UC(0x00B5), UC(0x03A9), UC(0x03BB), UC(0x03B1), UC(0x03B2),
        UC(0x00B0), UC(0x2030), UC(0x00B9), UC(0x00B2), UC(0x00B3), UC(0x2070), UC(0x00BD), UC(0x00BC), UC(0x00BE), UC(0x2300),
        UC(0x2026), UC(0x2022), UC(0x00B7), UC(0x2013), UC(0x2014), UC(0x2010), UC(0x201C), UC(0x201D), UC(0x2018), UC(0x2019),
        UC(0x2190), UC(0x2191), UC(0x2192), UC(0x2193), UC(0x2194), UC(0x2195), UC(0x2196), UC(0x2197), UC(0x2198), UC(0x2199),
        UC(0x21D0), UC(0x21D2), UC(0x21D1), UC(0x21D3), UC(0x21A9), UC(0x21AA), UC(0x21BA), UC(0x21BB), UC(0x2934), UC(0x2935),
        UC(0x2713), UC(0x2714), UC(0x2715), UC(0x2716), UC(0x2611), UC(0x2610), UC(0x2612), UC(0x2605), UC(0x2606), UC(0x203B),
        UC(0x2660), UC(0x2665), UC(0x2666), UC(0x2663), UC(0x266A), UC(0x266B), UC(0x263A), UC(0x2639), UC(0x2642), UC(0x2640)
    )
};
 
Build it later with:
cd ~/c100-dev/c100-symbol-pad
make full QMK_HOME=../qmk_firmware
A successful build produced:
Linking: .build/keychron_c100_8k_symbol_pad.elf [OK]
Creating binary load file for flashing: .build/keychron_c100_8k_symbol_pad.bin [OK]
Creating load file for flashing: .build/keychron_c100_8k_symbol_pad.hex [OK]
The binary is:
~/c100-dev/qmk_firmware/.build/keychron_c100_8k_symbol_pad.bin
The original successful binary was 59,584 bytes. Do not treat that size as a permanent requirement; it is just a useful historical sanity check.

11. If make complains that files are from the future
When the project was copied from Windows into WSL, make warned that the Makefile and other files had modification times thousands of seconds in the future.
Normalize the timestamps:
cd ~/c100-dev/c100-symbol-pad
find . -type f -exec touch {} +
Then build again.

12. If arm-none-eabi-gcc is missing
Symptom:
/bin/sh: 1: arm-none-eabi-gcc: not found
Fix:
sudo apt update
sudo apt install gcc-arm-none-eabi binutils-arm-none-eabi libnewlib-arm-none-eabi
Then verify:
arm-none-eabi-gcc --version
and rebuild.

13. If dfu-suffix is missing during the build
Symptom:
dfu-suffix: not found
The compiler may already have produced the .bin, but QMK still treats the build as failed.
Fix:
sudo apt install dfu-util
Then:
dfu-suffix --version
and rebuild.

14. Windows DFU driver — Zadig
The C100 successfully entered DFU but originally appeared as:
USB device connected (NO DRIVER): DFU in FS Mode (2E3C:DF11:0200)
The fix was Zadig.
Get Zadig from:
zadig.akeo.ie/
It is a standalone Windows executable.
Run Zadig as Administrator while the C100 is in DFU mode.

Options → List All Devices
Select DFU in FS Mode
VERIFY THE USB ID IS 2E3C:DF11
Select WinUSB
Install / Replace Driver

Afterward, the device showed:
USB device connected (WinUSB): (Undefined Vendor) DFU in FS Mode (2E3C:DF11:0200)


                  
                  CAUTION
                  
                

Only change the driver for the DFU in FS Mode device with VID:PID 2E3C:DF11.
Do not replace the driver for the C100’s normal keyboard interface or some unrelated USB device.


QMK Toolbox was useful for seeing the device/driver state, but its Flash button remained unavailable for this AT32 DFU workflow. The actual successful flashing path was dfu-util inside WSL.

15. Install Windows USB passthrough for WSL
dfu-util runs inside WSL, but the DFU USB device initially belongs to Windows. Use usbipd-win to pass it through.
In Windows PowerShell as Administrator:
winget install --interactive --exact dorssel.usbipd-win
If just installed, reopen PowerShell afterward.
Important: usbipd commands below are Windows PowerShell commands, not WSL commands.
If you accidentally run usbipd list inside WSL and see warnings about missing linux-tools-...-WSL2, you are on the wrong side. Do not install those packages for this procedure. Switch back to Windows PowerShell.

16. Enter DFU and attach it to WSL
First put the keyboard in DFU mode:

Unplug C100.
Hold physical top-left key.
Plug C100 in.
Release after a couple seconds.

Then in Windows PowerShell as Administrator:
usbipd list
Find:
2e3c:df11  DFU in FS Mode
The original machine showed BUSID:
1-1
Do not assume it will always be 1-1. Use whatever BUSID usbipd list reports.
The first time, bind/share it:
usbipd bind --busid 1-1
Then attach it to WSL:
usbipd attach --wsl --busid 1-1
Successful attach output looked like:
usbipd: info: Using WSL distribution 'Ubuntu' to attach; the device will be available in all WSL 2 distributions.
usbipd: info: Detected networking mode 'nat'.
usbipd: info: Using IP address ... to reach the host.
The bind generally persists, so on later flashes only attach may be necessary. If attach says the device is not shared/bound, run bind again.

17. Verify the device inside WSL
Back in WSL:
lsusb
Expected:
2e3c:df11 Artery-Tech DFU in FS Mode
Then:
sudo dfu-util -l
Using sudo matters. Without it, the original attempt returned:
LIBUSB_ERROR_ACCESS
The correct enumeration looked like:
Found DFU: [2e3c:df11] ... alt=1, name="@Option byte   /0x1FFFF800/01*512g", serial="AT32"
Found DFU: [2e3c:df11] ... alt=0, name="@Internal Flash   /0x08000000/128*002Kg", serial="AT32"
The important target is:
alt=0
@Internal Flash
0x08000000
Do not flash the option-byte target (alt=1).

18. Flash the safe one-key test
Only after the one-key test firmware successfully builds and DFU enumeration looks correct:
sudo dfu-util \
  -a 0 \
  -d 2e3c:df11 \
  -s 0x08000000:leave \
  -D ~/c100-dev/qmk_firmware/.build/keychron_c100_8k_unicode_test.bin
The successful output looked like:
Opening DFU capable USB device...
Device ID 2e3c:df11
Setting Alternate Interface #0 ...
DfuSe interface name: "Internal Flash   "
Downloading element to address = 0x08000000
Erase    done.
Download done.
File downloaded successfully
Submitting leave request...
Transitioning to dfuMANIFEST state
The keyboard should reboot out of DFU.
Open Notepad and press physical top-left.
Expected:
©
The original proof-of-concept produced:
©©©©©©©©©©©©
because, naturally, the button had to be pressed a bunch of times.
If © works, QMK Unicode + Windows HexNumpad is working.

19. Build and flash the full 100-key version
Build:
cd ~/c100-dev/c100-symbol-pad
make full QMK_HOME=../qmk_firmware
Confirm the binary exists:
ls -lh ~/c100-dev/qmk_firmware/.build/keychron_c100_8k_symbol_pad.bin
Enter DFU using the normal physical top-left-key-on-connect method again.
In Windows Admin PowerShell:
usbipd list
Use the current BUSID and attach:
usbipd attach --wsl --busid 1-1
Back in WSL:
lsusb
sudo dfu-util -l
Confirm alt=0 is still @Internal Flash /0x08000000....
Then flash:
sudo dfu-util \
  -a 0 \
  -d 2e3c:df11 \
  -s 0x08000000:leave \
  -D ~/c100-dev/qmk_firmware/.build/keychron_c100_8k_symbol_pad.bin
Wait for:
Erase done.
Download done.
File downloaded successfully
Submitting leave request...
Transitioning to dfuMANIFEST state

20. Final validation
Open Notepad and press every key from top-left to bottom-right.
The exact successful output was:
©®™℠℗§¶№†‡
¢£€¥₹₩₽₺₴₿
±×÷≠≈≤≥∞√∫
∑∏∂∆πµΩλαβ
°‰¹²³⁰½¼¾⌀
…•·–—‐“”‘’
←↑→↓↔↕↖↗↘↙
⇐⇒⇑⇓↩↪↺↻⤴⤵
✓✔✕✖☑☐☒★☆※
♠♥♦♣♪♫☺☹♂♀
If those ten rows appear exactly, the firmware is working.

21. Quick rebuild / reflash cheat sheet
Assuming the machine is already configured and the source tree still exists:
Build
cd ~/c100-dev/c100-symbol-pad
make full QMK_HOME=../qmk_firmware
Enter DFU
Unplug → hold PHYSICAL top-left key → reconnect USB → release
Windows Admin PowerShell
usbipd list
usbipd attach --wsl --busid <CURRENT-BUSID>
If required:
usbipd bind --busid <CURRENT-BUSID>
usbipd attach --wsl --busid <CURRENT-BUSID>
WSL
lsusb
sudo dfu-util -l
Verify:
2e3c:df11
alt=0
@Internal Flash
0x08000000
Then:
sudo dfu-util \
  -a 0 \
  -d 2e3c:df11 \
  -s 0x08000000:leave \
  -D ~/c100-dev/qmk_firmware/.build/keychron_c100_8k_symbol_pad.bin

22. Troubleshooting history

















































ProblemWhat fixed itarm-none-eabi-gcc: not foundInstall gcc-arm-none-eabi binutils-arm-none-eabi libnewlib-arm-none-eabidfu-suffix: not foundInstall dfu-utilFiles reported modification times in the futurefind . -type f -exec touch {} +C100 enters DFU but Windows/QMK Toolbox says NO DRIVERZadig → DFU in FS Mode 2E3C:DF11 → WinUSBQMK Toolbox sees AT32 DFU but Flash is disabledUse dfu-util through WSL insteadRunning usbipd in WSL gives missing WSL kernel tools warningRun usbipd from Windows PowerShell, not WSLWSL lsusb cannot see C100 DFUusbipd bind / usbipd attach --wsl from Windowsdfu-util -l gives LIBUSB_ERROR_ACCESSRun it as sudo dfu-util -lUnsure which DFU target to flashUse alt 0 Internal Flash at 0x08000000, never alt 1 Option byteNeed to recover after custom firmwareUnplug → hold physical top-left → reconnect; confirmed working

23. Things deliberately NOT implemented
These were considered and rejected:

16 Keychron Launcher macros: not enough for 100 symbols.
100 Alt-code macros: Launcher only exposes 16 macro slots.
Direct Unicode keycodes in Launcher JSON: the stock C100 firmware did not have the necessary QMK Unicode feature enabled, so the experiment did not work.
AutoHotkey: would work, but would make the keyboard dependent on a Windows-side script.
Dedicated DFU key in the final map: unnecessary.
Two-key DFU combo: unnecessary.
Changing the default/top-left DFU recovery behavior: explicitly not wanted.
Numpad block: abandoned so all 100 physical keys could be unique symbols.


24. Why this works
The stock Keychron Launcher is only a configuration layer over whatever functionality was compiled into the keyboard firmware.
The custom firmware changes the firmware itself.
QMK’s Unicode feature converts a key such as:
UC(0x2605)
into the Windows Unicode input sequence required to produce:
★
That means all 100 symbols can exist as real firmware key behaviors without consuming Keychron Launcher macro slots.

25. Backup checklist for Future Me
Keep copies of:

this Markdown note
the complete c100-symbol-pad source directory
the exact working keychron_c100_8k_symbol_pad.bin
the one-key keychron_c100_8k_unicode_test.bin
the 10×10 symbol/keycap artwork
if convenient, a copy or commit reference for the Keychron qmk_firmware source used to build it

The Git branch used on 2026-09-16 was:
Keychron/qmk_firmware
branch: 2025q3
target: keychron/c100_8k
Twenty years from now that branch, dependencies, URLs, or toolchain may no longer exist in the same form. Keeping the source tree and known-good .bin locally is much safer than relying only on today’s GitHub state.

26. One-line summary
Build Keychron C100 QMK firmware with UNICODE_ENABLE = yes, put the C100 into DFU by holding the physical top-left key while connecting USB, pass 2e3c:df11 into WSL with usbipd-win, then flash alt=0 at 0x08000000 with dfu-util.

projects/obsidian-vault-to-website/guide.title: Obsidian-to-Website-General-Guide
projects/obsidian-vault-to-website/guide.content:
Build Your Own Obsidian-Powered Wiki/Blog Website
This guide shows one way to turn an Obsidian vault into a public website while keeping the vault itself as the permanent source of truth.
The basic idea is simple:
Write locally in Obsidian. Keep everything in Git. Publish only the notes you explicitly mark public. Build a static website from those notes. Push everything to one private GitHub repository. Let the web server pull the repo and serve only the generated site.
The website is disposable.
The Markdown vault is not.

What You End Up With
On your personal computer:
Your Vault
├── Projects/
├── Updates/
├── Welcome.md
├── .obsidian/
├── .git/
└── .site/
    └── public/        <-- generated website
Beside it:
Quartz/
├── content/           <-- temporary/generated staging content
├── public/            <-- Quartz build output
├── Publish-Site.ps1
└── Quartz files...
In GitHub:
One private repository
├── your full vault
└── .site/public
On the web server:
C:\Repos\MySite\       <-- private Git checkout
└── .site\public
 
C:\xampp\htdocs\mysite <-- only public website files
The publishing flow looks like this:
OBSIDIAN
   ↓
Markdown vault
   ↓
Generate indexes
   ↓
Select publish:true notes
   ↓
Copy referenced assets
   ↓
Quartz build
   ↓
.site/public
   ↓
Git commit + push
   ↓
Private GitHub repo
   ↓
Web server git pull
   ↓
Copy .site/public into Apache web root
   ↓
Internet

1. Why Structure It This Way?
You could technically make the Obsidian vault itself the website source directory.
Don’t.
A better approach is:
Vault = permanent source
Website = generated view
This gives you several advantages:

your notes remain ordinary Markdown files;
you can change static-site generators later;
private notes never need to enter the public build;
your original images remain untouched;
Git tracks the history of your diary/wiki;
GitHub becomes an off-machine backup;
the web server does not need Obsidian;
the web server does not even need Node or Quartz if you build on your home PC.

If the website disappears tomorrow, your vault is still fine.

2. Install the Required Software
On the computer where you write and build the site, install:

Obsidian
Git
Node.js 22 or newer
npm

Check them:
node -v
npm -v
git --version
You should also have a GitHub account.
If you plan to self-host on Windows with Apache, this guide assumes something like XAMPP, but any ordinary static web server will work.

3. Create Your Obsidian Vault
Create an Obsidian vault anywhere you like.
Example:
D:\Notes\My Lab
A simple starting structure might be:
My Lab/
├── Projects/
│   └── Projects Home.md
├── Updates/
│   └── Updates Home.md
├── Assets/
└── Welcome.md
Do not over-design the folder structure.
Let it grow based on how you actually use it.

4. Use a Simple Content Model
A useful model is:

Updates = chronological posts
Projects = persistent wiki-style subjects

For example:
Projects/
└── Custom Keyboard/
    ├── Custom Keyboard Home.md
    ├── Guides/
    └── Assets/
 
Updates/
├── 2026-09-01 - Started the Keyboard Project.md
├── 2026-09-05 - Firmware Finally Works.md
└── Updates Home.md
Use ISO dates:
YYYY-MM-DD
instead of:
M.D.YYYY
because ISO dates sort correctly as plain text.

5. Add Frontmatter
Use YAML frontmatter to tell the publishing script what a note is.
Update
---
type: update
date: 2026-09-19
project: Custom Keyboard
publish: true
---
Project Home
---
type: project
project: Custom Keyboard
status: active
publish: true
---
Homepage
---
title: Welcome
publish: true
---
The important property is:
publish: true
Anything without that property stays out of the public build.
That gives you an explicit privacy model:
No publish:true
    = private
 
publish:true
    = public

6. Put the Vault Under Git
Open PowerShell.
If your path contains square brackets, use -LiteralPath.
Example:
Set-Location -LiteralPath "D:\Notes\My Lab"
Initialize Git:
git init
git branch -M main
Create a .gitignore:
.obsidian/workspace.json
.obsidian/workspace-mobile.json
.trash/
Thumbs.db
.DS_Store
desktop.ini
Do not automatically ignore the whole .obsidian directory.
Keeping lightweight Obsidian settings in Git can make restoring the vault easier.
Then:
git add .
git commit -m "Initial vault"

7. Create a Private GitHub Repository
Create a new private GitHub repository.
Do not initialize it with a README, license, or .gitignore if your local repository already exists.
Then connect your local vault:
git remote add origin github.com/YOURNAME/YOUR-REPO.git
git push -u origin main
Because the repository contains your full vault, keep it private unless you intentionally want every note public.

8. Install Quartz
Create a separate directory for Quartz.
Example:
D:\Notes\
├── My Lab\
└── MyLab-Web\
Clone Quartz:
git clone github.com/jackyzha0/quartz.git "D:\Notes\MyLab-Web"
Then:
Set-Location -LiteralPath "D:\Notes\MyLab-Web"
npm install
Initialize Quartz for Obsidian-style Markdown:
npx quartz create --template obsidian --strategy new --baseUrl example.com/lab
If the default theme package is missing and Quartz complains about:
Cannot find module '@quartz-themes/default'
install it:
npm install @quartz-themes/default
In quartz.config.yaml, set at least:
configuration:
  pageTitle: "My Lab"
  baseUrl: "example.com/lab"

9. Do Not Point Quartz Directly At Your Vault
Instead, use a staging directory:
Quartz\content
Your publishing script should recreate this directory every time.
That script can:

scan the vault;
generate your automatic index pages;
select only publish: true notes;
copy those notes into Quartz;
copy only the assets referenced by those public notes;
rename Welcome.md to index.md;
run Quartz;
copy the final website into .site/public inside the vault repository.

This gives you a hard boundary between:
private source
and:
public build

10. Auto-Generate Updates Home
Instead of manually maintaining:
Updates Home.md
generate it from frontmatter.
The generator should:
find all notes where:
type = update
publish = true
then sort by:
date descending
and output something like:
---
title: Updates Home
type: index
publish: true
---
 
# Latest Updates
 
- [[Updates/2026-09-19 - Built My Website|2026-09-19 - Built My Website]]
- [[Updates/2026-09-18 - Fixed My Server|2026-09-18 - Fixed My Server]]
- [[Updates/2026-09-17 - Started Something Weird|2026-09-17 - Started Something Weird]]
Now every new update appears automatically.

11. Auto-Generate Projects Home
The same idea works for projects.
Find all notes where:
type = project
publish = true
Then find the newest Update where:
project: Exact Same Project Name
and sort the projects by most recent activity.
That gives you:
# Projects
 
- [[Projects/Custom Keyboard/Custom Keyboard Home|Custom Keyboard]] — last activity 2026-09-19
- [[Projects/Game Server/Game Server Home|Game Server]] — last activity 2026-09-17
- [[Projects/Retro Computer/Retro Computer Home|Retro Computer]] — last activity 2026-09-12
You write the content.
The script handles the bookkeeping.

12. Store the Generated Site in the Same Repository
After Quartz builds:
Quartz\public
copy that into:
Your Vault\.site\public
Now your single repository contains:
source notes
+
generated website
This means the web server can get everything it needs with one:
git pull
while Apache still exposes only the generated site.

13. A Simple Home-PC Publishing Wrapper
Create:
Publish-Site.bat
with something like:
@echo off
setlocal
 
set "PUBLISHER=D:\Notes\MyLab-Web\Publish-Site.ps1"
 
echo.
echo ========================================
echo   Publishing Site
echo ========================================
echo.
 
if not exist "%PUBLISHER%" (
    echo ERROR: Publisher script not found:
    echo   %PUBLISHER%
    pause
    exit /b 1
)
 
powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File "%PUBLISHER%"
 
if errorlevel 1 (
    echo.
    echo PUBLISH FAILED
    pause
    exit /b 1
)
 
echo.
echo Publish complete.
echo.
pause
The PowerShell publisher itself should:
generate indexes
build staging content
run Quartz
copy Quartz public output to .site/public
git add
git commit
git push
Once that works, publishing becomes one double-click.

14. Web Server Layout
Do not clone the full private repository directly into your Apache public directory.
Instead use:
C:\Repos\MySite
for the private checkout.
Then have Apache serve:
C:\xampp\htdocs\mysite
The reason is simple:
Your Git repository contains private source notes.
Only:
.site\public
belongs on the public web.

15. Clone the Repo on the Web Server
On the web server:
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path "C:\Repos" -Force
Then:
git clone github.com/YOURNAME/YOUR-REPO.git "C:\Repos\MySite"
Verify:
Test-Path -LiteralPath "C:\Repos\MySite\.site\public\index.html"
Expected:
True

16. Create a Web-Host Update BAT
Example:
@echo off
setlocal
 
set "REPO_DIR=C:\Repos\MySite"
set "WEB_DIR=C:\xampp\htdocs\mysite"
set "SITE_DIR=%REPO_DIR%\.site\public"
 
echo.
echo ========================================
echo   Updating Website
echo ========================================
echo.
 
where git >nul 2>&1
if errorlevel 1 (
    echo ERROR: Git is not installed or is not in PATH.
    pause
    exit /b 1
)
 
if not exist "%REPO_DIR%\.git" (
    echo ERROR: Git repository not found:
    echo   %REPO_DIR%
    pause
    exit /b 1
)
 
cd /d "%REPO_DIR%"
 
git pull --ff-only origin main
 
if errorlevel 1 (
    echo ERROR: Git pull failed.
    pause
    exit /b 1
)
 
if not exist "%SITE_DIR%\index.html" (
    echo ERROR: Generated site not found:
    echo   %SITE_DIR%
    pause
    exit /b 1
)
 
if not exist "%WEB_DIR%" (
    mkdir "%WEB_DIR%"
)
 
robocopy "%SITE_DIR%" "%WEB_DIR%" /MIR /R:2 /W:1 /NFL /NDL /NP
 
if errorlevel 8 (
    echo ERROR: Website copy failed.
    pause
    exit /b 1
)
 
echo.
echo Site updated successfully.
echo.
pause
The important part is:
git pull
↓
copy .site/public
↓
Apache web directory

17. Why Use robocopy /MIR?
/MIR makes the live website exactly match the generated build.
That removes files that no longer exist in the site.
This is useful, but it also means:
Do not manually store unrelated files inside the site’s Apache directory.
They may be deleted during the next deployment.
Treat the live website directory as disposable.

18. Apache
If your existing Apache site already serves:
C:\xampp\htdocs
then putting your generated site at:
C:\xampp\htdocs\mysite
may immediately give you:
example.com/mysite/
If you prefer a subdomain, create a virtual host pointing directly at that directory.
Example:
<VirtualHost *:80>
    ServerName lab.example.com
 
    DocumentRoot "C:/xampp/htdocs/mysite"
 
    <Directory "C:/xampp/htdocs/mysite">
        AllowOverride All
        Require all granted
    </Directory>
</VirtualHost>
Always validate Apache before restarting:
C:\xampp\apache\bin\httpd.exe -t
You want:
Syntax OK

19. HTTPS with win-acme and Apache
For a Windows Apache server, win-acme can request Let’s Encrypt certificates and export PEM files.
Run wacs.exe as Administrator.
A common manual Apache setup is:
Create certificate (full options)
→ manually enter domain
→ single certificate
→ HTTP validation using filesystem path
→ web root of your Apache site
→ RSA
→ PEM encoded files
→ save into Apache cert directory
→ no password on private key
→ no additional store
→ no IIS install step
Example PEM location:
C:\xampp\apache\certs
Your Apache SSL config might contain:
SSLCertificateFile "C:/xampp/apache/certs/example.com-crt.pem"
SSLCertificateKeyFile "C:/xampp/apache/certs/example.com-key.pem"
SSLCertificateChainFile "C:/xampp/apache/certs/example.com-chain.pem"
After issuing or renewing:
C:\xampp\apache\bin\httpd.exe -t
Then restart Apache.
Make sure win-acme’s scheduled renewal task is healthy.
Otherwise you may discover the certificate expired only when your browser starts screaming at you six months later.

19.5. Make Quartz Clean URLs Work on Apache
Quartz normally generates links without .html.
For example, the browser may request:
example.com/mysite/updates/my-post
while the generated file is physically:
C:\xampp\htdocs\mysite\updates\my-post.html
Quartz’s development server handles this automatically.
Plain Apache usually needs a rewrite rule.
Create an .htaccess file in the parent web root or another directory that will not be overwritten by your deployment process.
For example, if the live generated site is mirrored into:
C:\xampp\htdocs\example\mysite
you can store the rewrite file at:
C:\xampp\htdocs\example\.htaccess
with:
RewriteEngine On
 
RewriteCond %{REQUEST_FILENAME} !-f
RewriteCond %{REQUEST_FILENAME} !-d
RewriteCond %{REQUEST_FILENAME}.html -f
RewriteRule ^(.+?)/?$ $1.html [L]
This means:
/mysite/updates/my-post
will internally serve:
/mysite/updates/my-post.html
without changing the visible URL.
Check that mod_rewrite is loaded:
C:\xampp\apache\bin\httpd.exe -M | findstr rewrite
Expected:
rewrite_module (shared)
The HTTPS vhost must allow .htaccess
A common gotcha is having AllowOverride All on the port-80 virtual host but not on the port-443 SSL virtual host.
If HTTP works but HTTPS clean links still return 404s, inspect the SSL vhost.
Inside the relevant <VirtualHost *:443> block, make sure the web root has a matching directory section:
<Directory "C:/xampp/htdocs/example">
    AllowOverride All
    Require all granted
</Directory>
Then validate:
C:\xampp\apache\bin\httpd.exe -t
and restart Apache.
A useful diagnostic is:
Test-Path -LiteralPath "C:\xampp\htdocs\example\mysite\updates\my-post.html"
If the .html file exists but the extensionless URL returns 404, the static build is probably fine and the problem is Apache routing.
20. Normal Daily Workflow
Once everything is configured, this should be boring.
On your personal PC
Write in Obsidian.
When something should be public:
publish: true
Then run:
Publish-Site.bat
That:
updates indexes
builds Quartz
updates .site/public
commits
pushes
On the web server
Run:
Update-Site.bat
That:
git pull
copies generated site
Done.

21. Troubleshooting
PowerShell cannot enter a folder containing [square brackets]
Use:
Set-Location -LiteralPath "D:\Some\[Folder]\Vault"
instead of:
cd "D:\Some\[Folder]\Vault"
Square brackets have wildcard meaning in PowerShell paths.

Quartz homepage is a 404
Quartz expects:
content\index.md
Your publisher should copy:
Welcome.md
to:
content\index.md

Homepage title says index
Give your homepage frontmatter:
---
title: Welcome
publish: true
---

Explorer is empty
Quartz probably received only one file.
Inspect:
Quartz\content
Your generated public notes should actually exist there before the build.

Graph View shows one lonely dot
Same issue.
One page in Quartz means one graph node.
Once linked notes are present, the graph becomes interesting.

A note is missing from the website
Check:
publish: true
Then rebuild.

A project is sorted incorrectly
Check that the Project Home and its Update posts use the same:
project: Project Name

Quartz cannot find @quartz-themes/default
Run:
npm install @quartz-themes/default

Windows PowerShell shows bizarre syntax errors in a script
Windows PowerShell 5.1 can be touchy about UTF-8 scripts without a BOM.
If a script suddenly claims normal lines contain broken syntax after a Unicode character, try:

saving the operational script as ASCII if possible;
saving it as UTF-8 with BOM;
or using modern PowerShell 7.

For small automation scripts, ASCII-only text is often the least surprising option.

git pull fails on the web server
Check:
git remote -v
git status
git branch
The server checkout should generally stay untouched except for git pull.
Avoid hand-editing files in the checkout.

22. Security Notes
A few things matter here.
Keep the repository private
If the repo contains your entire vault, it probably contains notes you never intended for the public internet.
The generated site may be public.
The repository does not need to be.
Keep the Git checkout outside the web root
Good:
C:\Repos\MySite
C:\xampp\htdocs\mysite
Bad:
C:\xampp\htdocs\mysite\.git
C:\xampp\htdocs\mysite\Private Notes
Do not rely on web-server defaults to protect private source files.
Use an explicit public flag
Prefer:
publish: true
over an “everything is public unless hidden” model.
Accidentally forgetting to publish something is annoying.
Accidentally publishing something private is worse.

23. Backup Philosophy
Think of the layers separately:
Obsidian vault
    = canonical source
 
Local Git
    = version history
 
Private GitHub
    = off-machine copy and transport
 
.site/public
    = generated website snapshot
 
Web-server checkout
    = deployment source
 
Apache web folder
    = disposable live copy
The one thing that should be treated as precious is:
the vault
Everything else should be reproducible from it.

24. Rebuilding After Disaster
If your web server dies:
clone repo
copy .site/public
configure Apache
restore HTTPS
If your personal PC dies:
clone repo
open vault in Obsidian
reinstall Quartz
restore publisher script
If Quartz disappears:
Use another static-site generator.
Your Markdown still exists.
That is the entire reason for structuring the system this way.

25. Final Checklist
A healthy setup should have all of these:

Obsidian opens the vault normally.
The vault is a Git repository.
The GitHub repository is private.
Public notes use publish: true.
Updates Home is generated.
Projects Home is generated.
Quartz builds successfully.
.site/public/index.html exists.
The home-PC publisher commits and pushes.
The web server can git pull.
The web server copies .site/public into the Apache directory.
Apache serves the site.
HTTPS works.
Quartz extensionless links resolve correctly through Apache.
The HTTPS vhost allows .htaccess overrides when rewrite rules are used.
Automatic certificate renewal is configured.

Once all of that works:
Stop touching the plumbing and go write things.

Shag’s Lab: The Doomsday Rebuild Guide
This is the file for Future Me, Curious You, or Whoever Is Looking At A Dead PC Wondering Why A Personal Wiki Needed A Build Pipeline.
The short version:
The Obsidian vault is the source of truth.
Everything else is replaceable.
The live site is a static Quartz build made from explicitly public notes in that vault. The vault and generated site live in one private Git repository. The home PC builds and pushes it. The web host pulls it and copies only the finished public files into Apache’s web root.
If every piece of software involved in this project vanished tomorrow, the important part would still be a folder full of Markdown files and images.
That is the point.
Current layout
Home PC
F:\[DIARY]\
├── Shag's Lab\                 <-- SOURCE OF TRUTH / Git repository
│   ├── .git\
│   ├── .obsidian\
│   ├── Projects\
│   ├── Updates\
│   ├── Welcome.md
│   └── .site\
│       └── public\             <-- generated static website, committed to Git
│
└── ShagsLab-Web\               <-- disposable Quartz/build machinery
    ├── content\                <-- regenerated staging content
    ├── public\                 <-- Quartz build output
    ├── Publish-Lab.ps1
    └── Quartz files...
GitHub
One private repository:
github.com/ToastSweat/shags-lab
It contains the vault and .site/public.
Keep it private because the repo contains the complete vault, not merely the public website.
Web host
C:\PGN\ShagsLab\                <-- private Git checkout
└── .site\public\               <-- finished site from home PC
 
C:\xampp\htdocs\helvete\lab\    <-- Apache PUBLIC directory
Public URL:
helvete.pizza/lab/
Apache serves only:
C:\xampp\htdocs\helvete\lab
The full Git checkout is intentionally kept outside htdocs.
The content model
Do not overcomplicate this.
There are two main things:

Updates are chronological diary entries.
Projects are persistent wiki-ish things.

An Update should normally have:
---
type: update
date: 2026-09-19
project: Exact Project Name
publish: true
---
A Project Home should normally have:
---
type: project
project: Exact Project Name
status: active
publish: true
---
The project: value on the Project Home and its Updates should match.
That is how the publisher knows which Updates belong to which Project and can sort Projects by recent activity.
The homepage should contain:
---
title: Welcome
publish: true
---
Updates/Updates Home.md and Projects/Projects Home.md are generated by the publisher.
Do not lovingly hand-maintain those lists. The script will overwrite them.
Anything without:
publish: true
stays out of the public build.
Normal publishing workflow
On the home PC:

Work normally in Obsidian.
Add/update notes.
Set publish: true only on things that should be public.
Run Publish-ShagsLab-HomePC.bat.

That BAT runs the PowerShell publisher.
The publisher:

Scans the vault.
Generates Updates Home.
Generates Projects Home.
Creates a clean Quartz staging directory.
Copies only published notes.
Copies assets referenced by published notes.
Turns Welcome.md into index.md.
Builds Quartz.
Mirrors the built static site into .site\public inside the vault repository.
Commits the vault and generated site.
Pushes main to GitHub.

Then, on the web host, run:
Update-ShagsLab-WebHost.bat
That:

Pulls origin/main.
Verifies .site\public\index.html exists.
Mirrors .site\public into C:\xampp\htdocs\helvete\lab.

Done.
Rebuilding the home PC from GitHub
If the home PC dies but GitHub survives:
1. Install the basics
Install:

Git
Node.js 22 or newer
npm
Obsidian

The setup was originally built with:
Node 24.14.1
npm 11.11.0
Git 2.53.0.windows.2
Quartz 5
Newer compatible versions are fine, but if Future Quartz has changed beyond recognition, use a compatible Quartz v5 release.
2. Recreate the diary directory
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path "F:\[DIARY]" -Force
Clone the private repo:
git clone github.com/ToastSweat/shags-lab.git "F:\[DIARY]\Shag's Lab"
Because [DIARY] contains square brackets, use PowerShell’s literal-path commands when navigating:
Set-Location -LiteralPath "F:\[DIARY]\Shag's Lab"
Do not rely on:
cd "F:\[DIARY]\Shag's Lab"
PowerShell may interpret the brackets as a wildcard pattern.
Open F:\[DIARY]\Shag's Lab as an Obsidian vault.
3. Recreate Quartz
Clone Quartz beside the vault:
git clone github.com/jackyzha0/quartz.git "F:\[DIARY]\ShagsLab-Web"
Set-Location -LiteralPath "F:\[DIARY]\ShagsLab-Web"
npm i
Initialize it for Obsidian:
npx quartz create --template obsidian --strategy new --baseUrl helvete.pizza/lab
If Quartz complains that the default theme exists but cannot be loaded:
Cannot find module '@quartz-themes/default'
install it explicitly:
npm install @quartz-themes/default
In quartz.config.yaml, make sure the important values are:
configuration:
  pageTitle: "Shag's Lab"
  baseUrl: "helvete.pizza/lab"
The custom publisher performs the public/private filtering before Quartz sees the notes, so the Quartz explicit-publish plugin does not need to be enabled.
Restore Publish-Lab.ps1 from the copy embedded later in this guide.
Save it as:
F:\[DIARY]\ShagsLab-Web\Publish-Lab.ps1
Restore the home-PC BAT from this guide as well.
Creating the Git repository from a surviving local vault
If GitHub is gone but the local vault survives:
Set-Location -LiteralPath "F:\[DIARY]\Shag's Lab"
 
git init
git branch -M main
Use this .gitignore:
.obsidian/workspace.json
.obsidian/workspace-mobile.json
.trash/
Thumbs.db
.DS_Store
desktop.ini
Do not ignore the whole .obsidian directory. The lightweight Obsidian configuration is useful when rebuilding the vault.
Then:
git add .
git commit -m "Initial Shag's Lab vault"
Create a new empty private GitHub repository and connect it:
git remote add origin github.com/ToastSweat/shags-lab.git
git push -u origin main
Rebuilding the web host
The web host does not build Quartz.
It only pulls the one private repo and copies the already-generated website into Apache’s public directory.
Install Git if necessary.
Create the non-public checkout location:
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path "C:\PGN" -Force
Clone:
git clone github.com/ToastSweat/shags-lab.git "C:\PGN\ShagsLab"
GitHub authentication may open a browser because the repository is private.
Verify the generated site came down:
Test-Path -LiteralPath "C:\PGN\ShagsLab\.site\public\index.html"
Expected:
True
Restore Update-ShagsLab-WebHost.bat from the copy later in this guide and run it.
It will create this directory if needed:
C:\xampp\htdocs\helvete\lab
and mirror the finished site into it.
Important warning about /MIR
The web-host BAT uses:
robocopy ... /MIR
That is intentional.
It makes the Apache directory exactly match the generated site and removes stale files.
Therefore:
Do not store unrelated hand-written files inside C:\xampp\htdocs\helvete\lab.
They may be deleted on the next update.
Testing the pipeline
Home PC
After publishing:
Test-Path -LiteralPath "F:\[DIARY]\Shag's Lab\.site\public\index.html"
Expected:
True
Check Git:
Set-Location -LiteralPath "F:\[DIARY]\Shag's Lab"
git status
git remote -v
After a successful publisher run, the working tree should normally be clean and origin should point at the private GitHub repo.
Web host
After running the updater:
Test-Path -LiteralPath "C:\xampp\htdocs\helvete\lab\index.html"
Expected:
True
Local Apache test:
http://localhost/lab/
Public test:
helvete.pizza/lab/
Apache and HTTPS
The site is a subdirectory of the existing helvete.pizza Apache site.
Live directory:
C:\xampp\htdocs\helvete\lab
The current certificate files for helvete.pizza are:
C:\xampp\apache\certs\helvete.pizza-crt.pem
C:\xampp\apache\certs\helvete.pizza-key.pem
C:\xampp\apache\certs\helvete.pizza-chain.pem
The Apache SSL configuration is in:
C:\xampp\apache\conf\extra\httpd-ssl.conf
Before restarting Apache after certificate/configuration changes:
C:\xampp\apache\bin\httpd.exe -t
Expected:
Syntax OK
Then restart Apache from the XAMPP Control Panel.
Reissuing the helvete.pizza certificate with win-acme
Run wacs.exe as Administrator.
The working manual setup used:

M - Create certificate (full options)
Manually input host name:
helvete.pizza

4 - Single certificate
1 - HTTP: save verification files on a path
Root path:
C:\xampp\htdocs\helvete

Do not copy the default web.config
2 - RSA key
2 - PEM encoded files
PEM destination:
C:\xampp\apache\certs

1 - No password on the private-key PEM
5 - No additional storage steps
3 - No additional installation steps

Successful output included:
Authorization result: valid
Exporting .pem files to C:\xampp\apache\certs
Scheduled task looks healthy
Certificate helvete.pizza created
Then validate Apache and restart it.
If the old renewal dies with an ARI replaces error
The broken old renewal produced an error similar to:
Failed to create order:
Could not validate ARI 'replaces' field
Repeatedly running the bad renewal did not fix it.
Creating a fresh certificate using the steps above did.
Afterward, open:
A: Manage renewals
Select only the old errored helvete.pizza renewal and choose:
C: Cancel renewal
Do not revoke the certificate merely to remove a dead renewal definition.
Keep the healthy safecracker.helvete.pizza renewal and the new healthy helvete.pizza renewal.
Metadata troubleshooting
If an Update does not appear on Updates Home, verify:
type: update
date: YYYY-MM-DD
publish: true
If a Project does not sort based on its newest Update, verify the Project Home and Update use exactly the same project: value.
Example:
Project Home:
project: Keychron C100
Update:
project: Keychron C100
If they differ, the generator treats them as different projects.
If a note appears in Obsidian but not publicly, verify it has:
publish: true
That omission is a feature, not a bug.
Quartz troubleshooting
Homepage is a 404
Quartz expects:
content\index.md
The publisher creates it from Welcome.md.
Verify Welcome.md contains:
---
title: Welcome
publish: true
---
Then rerun the publisher.
Homepage is titled index
Same issue: make sure the title: Welcome frontmatter is present before building.
Explorer is empty and Graph View is one dot
Quartz has only received one note, usually because content was manually populated incorrectly.
Do not manually maintain ShagsLab-Web\content.
Run the publisher so it regenerates the staging directory from the vault.
@quartz-themes/default cannot be found
From:
F:\[DIARY]\ShagsLab-Web
run:
npm install @quartz-themes/default
then rebuild.
Windows PowerShell throws bizarre parse errors around normal code
The publisher must remain safe for Windows PowerShell 5.1.
The original failure came from a Unicode em dash in a UTF-8-without-BOM .ps1, which PowerShell misread and then produced a cascade of nonsense parser errors.
Keep the operational publisher script ASCII-only unless PowerShell encoding behavior is deliberately changed.
The actual backup philosophy
There are several layers here and they have different jobs:
Obsidian vault
    = original source
 
Local Git
    = local history
 
Private GitHub
    = off-machine copy + transport
 
.site\public
    = generated website snapshot
 
Web host checkout
    = deploy source
 
Apache lab folder
    = disposable live copy
The most important data is always:
F:\[DIARY]\Shag's Lab
If the website disappears, rebuild it.
If Apache disappears, rebuild it.
If Quartz disappears, replace it with something else.
Do not contort the vault around the website.
The website exists to present the vault.
The vault does not exist to feed the website.

Recovery scripts
The following are the working scripts used by this setup as of September 19, 2026.
Keep this guide under source control so Future Me can recreate them even if the operational copies are gone.
Publish-Lab.ps1
Save as:
F:\[DIARY]\ShagsLab-Web\Publish-Lab.ps1
param(
    [string]$VaultPath = "F:\[DIARY]\Shag's Lab",
    [string]$QuartzRoot = "F:\[DIARY]\ShagsLab-Web",
    [string]$TrackedSiteRoot = "F:\[DIARY]\Shag's Lab\.site\public",
    [switch]$Serve,
    [switch]$SkipGit
)
 
$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
 
function Write-Step {
    param([string]$Message)
    Write-Host ""
    Write-Host "==> $Message" -ForegroundColor Cyan
}
 
function Write-Utf8NoBom {
    param(
        [string]$Path,
        [string]$Text
    )
    $parent = Split-Path -Parent $Path
    if ($parent -and -not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $parent)) {
        New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $parent -Force | Out-Null
    }
    $utf8 = New-Object System.Text.UTF8Encoding($false)
    [System.IO.File]::WriteAllText($Path, $Text, $utf8)
}
 
function Get-RelativePathFromRoot {
    param(
        [string]$Root,
        [string]$FullPath
    )
    $rootNormalized = $Root.TrimEnd('\')
    if (-not $FullPath.StartsWith($rootNormalized, [System.StringComparison]::OrdinalIgnoreCase)) {
        throw "Path '$FullPath' is not inside '$Root'."
    }
    return $FullPath.Substring($rootNormalized.Length).TrimStart('\')
}
 
function Get-FrontMatter {
    param([string]$Text)
 
    $result = @{}
    $normalized = $Text -replace "`r`n", "`n"
 
    if (-not $normalized.StartsWith("---`n")) {
        return $result
    }
 
    $end = $normalized.IndexOf("`n---`n", 4)
    if ($end -lt 0) {
        return $result
    }
 
    $block = $normalized.Substring(4, $end - 4)
 
    foreach ($line in ($block -split "`n")) {
        if ($line -match '^\s*([A-Za-z0-9_-]+)\s*:\s*(.*?)\s*$') {
            $key = $Matches[1].ToLowerInvariant()
            $value = $Matches[2].Trim()
 
            if (($value.StartsWith('"') -and $value.EndsWith('"')) -or
                ($value.StartsWith("'") -and $value.EndsWith("'"))) {
                $value = $value.Substring(1, $value.Length - 2)
            }
 
            $result[$key] = $value
        }
    }
 
    return $result
}
 
function Convert-ToDate {
    param([string]$Value)
 
    if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($Value)) {
        return [datetime]::MinValue
    }
 
    try {
        return [datetime]::Parse($Value, [System.Globalization.CultureInfo]::InvariantCulture)
    }
    catch {
        return [datetime]::MinValue
    }
}
 
function Get-ProjectKeysFromUpdate {
    param([string]$ProjectValue)
 
    if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($ProjectValue)) {
        return @()
    }
 
    # Supports the current simple format:
    # project: Keychron C100
    # project: BASS VI - Penny, GitHub
    return @(
        $ProjectValue -split ',' |
        ForEach-Object { $_.Trim() } |
        Where-Object { $_ }
    )
}
 
function Get-WikiTarget {
    param([string]$RawTarget)
 
    $target = $RawTarget.Trim()
 
    if ($target.Contains('|')) {
        $target = $target.Split('|')[0]
    }
    if ($target.Contains('#')) {
        $target = $target.Split('#')[0]
    }
 
    return $target.Trim()
}
 
if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $VaultPath -PathType Container)) {
    throw "Vault not found: $VaultPath"
}
if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $QuartzRoot -PathType Container)) {
    throw "Quartz root not found: $QuartzRoot"
}
 
$ContentRoot = Join-Path $QuartzRoot "content"
$PublicRoot = Join-Path $QuartzRoot "public"
 
Write-Step "Scanning Shag's Lab"
 
$noteFiles = Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $VaultPath -Recurse -File -Filter "*.md" |
    Where-Object {
        $_.FullName -notmatch '\\\.git\\' -and
        $_.FullName -notmatch '\\\.obsidian\\' -and
        $_.FullName -notmatch '\\\.trash\\'
    }
 
$notes = foreach ($file in $noteFiles) {
    $text = Get-Content -LiteralPath $file.FullName -Raw
    $fm = Get-FrontMatter -Text $text
 
    $publish = $false
    if ($fm.ContainsKey("publish")) {
        $publish = $fm["publish"].ToLowerInvariant() -eq "true"
    }
 
    $draft = $false
    if ($fm.ContainsKey("draft")) {
        $draft = $fm["draft"].ToLowerInvariant() -eq "true"
    }
 
    $type = if ($fm.ContainsKey("type")) { $fm["type"].ToLowerInvariant() } else { "" }
    $title = if ($fm.ContainsKey("title")) { $fm["title"] } else { $file.BaseName }
    $dateRaw = if ($fm.ContainsKey("date")) { $fm["date"] } else { "" }
    $project = if ($fm.ContainsKey("project")) { $fm["project"] } else { "" }
    $status = if ($fm.ContainsKey("status")) { $fm["status"] } else { "" }
 
    [pscustomobject]@{
        Source       = $file.FullName
        Relative     = Get-RelativePathFromRoot -Root $VaultPath -FullPath $file.FullName
        Directory    = $file.DirectoryName
        Name         = $file.BaseName
        Text         = $text
        FrontMatter  = $fm
        Publish      = ($publish -and -not $draft)
        Type         = $type
        Title        = $title
        DateRaw      = $dateRaw
        DateValue    = Convert-ToDate -Value $dateRaw
        Project      = $project
        Status       = $status
        Modified     = $file.LastWriteTime
    }
}
 
$publicUpdates = @(
    $notes |
    Where-Object { $_.Publish -and $_.Type -eq "update" } |
    Sort-Object @{ Expression = { $_.DateValue }; Descending = $true },
                @{ Expression = { $_.Name }; Descending = $true }
)
 
$publicProjects = @(
    $notes |
    Where-Object { $_.Publish -and $_.Type -eq "project" }
)
 
Write-Step "Generating Updates Home"
 
$updatesLines = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[string]
$updatesLines.Add("---")
$updatesLines.Add("title: Updates Home")
$updatesLines.Add("type: index")
$updatesLines.Add("publish: true")
$updatesLines.Add("---")
$updatesLines.Add("")
$updatesLines.Add("*This page is auto-generated.*")
$updatesLines.Add("")
$updatesLines.Add("## Latest Updates")
$updatesLines.Add("")
 
foreach ($update in $publicUpdates) {
    $target = ($update.Relative -replace '\\', '/') -replace '\.md$', ''
    $updatesLines.Add("- [[$target|$($update.Name)]]")
}
 
if ($publicUpdates.Count -eq 0) {
    $updatesLines.Add("_No published updates yet._")
}
 
if ($publicUpdates.Count -gt 0) {
    $updatesLines.Add("")
    $updatesLines.Add("*Last Updated: $($publicUpdates[0].DateValue.ToString('yyyy-MM-dd'))*")
}
 
$updatesHomePath = Join-Path $VaultPath "Updates\Updates Home.md"
Write-Utf8NoBom -Path $updatesHomePath -Text (($updatesLines -join "`r`n") + "`r`n")
 
Write-Step "Generating Projects Home"
 
$projectRows = foreach ($projectNote in $publicProjects) {
    $displayName = $projectNote.Title
    if ($displayName -eq $projectNote.Name) {
        $displayName = $displayName -replace '\s+Home$', ''
    }
 
    $projectKey = if (-not [string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($projectNote.Project)) {
        $projectNote.Project
    }
    else {
        $displayName
    }
 
    $matchingUpdates = @(
        $publicUpdates | Where-Object {
            $keys = Get-ProjectKeysFromUpdate -ProjectValue $_.Project
            $keys | Where-Object { $_ -ieq $projectKey }
        }
    )
 
    if ($matchingUpdates.Count -gt 0) {
        $activityDate = ($matchingUpdates | Sort-Object DateValue -Descending | Select-Object -First 1).DateValue
    }
    else {
        $activityDate = $projectNote.Modified
        Write-Warning "No published update matched project '$projectKey'. Using the project note's modified date. Add 'project: $projectKey' to the project Home note and use the same value on its update posts for exact sorting."
    }
 
    [pscustomobject]@{
        Note         = $projectNote
        DisplayName  = $displayName
        ProjectKey   = $projectKey
        ActivityDate = $activityDate
    }
}
 
$projectRows = @(
    $projectRows |
    Sort-Object @{ Expression = { $_.ActivityDate }; Descending = $true },
                @{ Expression = { $_.DisplayName }; Descending = $false }
)
 
$projectsLines = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[string]
$projectsLines.Add("---")
$projectsLines.Add("title: Projects Home")
$projectsLines.Add("type: index")
$projectsLines.Add("publish: true")
$projectsLines.Add("---")
$projectsLines.Add("")
$projectsLines.Add("*This page is auto-generated.*")
$projectsLines.Add("")
$projectsLines.Add("## Projects")
$projectsLines.Add("")
 
foreach ($row in $projectRows) {
    $target = ($row.Note.Relative -replace '\\', '/') -replace '\.md$', ''
    $dateText = $row.ActivityDate.ToString("yyyy-MM-dd")
    $projectsLines.Add("- [[$target|$($row.DisplayName)]] - last activity $dateText")
}
 
if ($projectRows.Count -eq 0) {
    $projectsLines.Add("_No published projects yet._")
}
 
if ($projectRows.Count -gt 0) {
    $projectsLines.Add("")
    $projectsLines.Add("*Last Updated: $($projectRows[0].ActivityDate.ToString('yyyy-MM-dd'))*")
}
 
$projectsHomePath = Join-Path $VaultPath "Projects\Projects Home.md"
Write-Utf8NoBom -Path $projectsHomePath -Text (($projectsLines -join "`r`n") + "`r`n")
 
# Re-scan so the freshly generated Home pages are included.
$noteFiles = Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $VaultPath -Recurse -File -Filter "*.md" |
    Where-Object {
        $_.FullName -notmatch '\\\.git\\' -and
        $_.FullName -notmatch '\\\.obsidian\\' -and
        $_.FullName -notmatch '\\\.trash\\'
    }
 
$notes = foreach ($file in $noteFiles) {
    $text = Get-Content -LiteralPath $file.FullName -Raw
    $fm = Get-FrontMatter -Text $text
 
    $publish = $false
    if ($fm.ContainsKey("publish")) {
        $publish = $fm["publish"].ToLowerInvariant() -eq "true"
    }
 
    $draft = $false
    if ($fm.ContainsKey("draft")) {
        $draft = $fm["draft"].ToLowerInvariant() -eq "true"
    }
 
    [pscustomobject]@{
        Source      = $file.FullName
        Relative    = Get-RelativePathFromRoot -Root $VaultPath -FullPath $file.FullName
        Directory   = $file.DirectoryName
        Name        = $file.BaseName
        Text        = $text
        Publish     = ($publish -and -not $draft)
    }
}
 
Write-Step "Creating clean public staging copy"
 
if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $ContentRoot) {
    Remove-Item -LiteralPath $ContentRoot -Recurse -Force
}
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $ContentRoot -Force | Out-Null
 
$publishedNotes = @($notes | Where-Object { $_.Publish })
 
$welcome = $publishedNotes | Where-Object { $_.Relative -ieq "Welcome.md" } | Select-Object -First 1
if (-not $welcome) {
    throw "Welcome.md must contain 'publish: true'. It becomes the public site's index.md."
}
 
foreach ($note in $publishedNotes) {
    if ($note.Relative -ieq "Welcome.md") {
        $destination = Join-Path $ContentRoot "index.md"
    }
    else {
        $destination = Join-Path $ContentRoot $note.Relative
    }
 
    $parent = Split-Path -Parent $destination
    if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $parent)) {
        New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $parent -Force | Out-Null
    }
 
    Copy-Item -LiteralPath $note.Source -Destination $destination -Force
}
 
# Build an index of non-Markdown files so only attachments actually referenced
# by published notes are copied into the website staging area.
$assetFiles = Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $VaultPath -Recurse -File |
    Where-Object {
        $_.Extension -ine ".md" -and
        $_.FullName -notmatch '\\\.git\\' -and
        $_.FullName -notmatch '\\\.obsidian\\' -and
        $_.FullName -notmatch '\\\.trash\\'
    }
 
$assetsByName = @{}
foreach ($asset in $assetFiles) {
    $key = $asset.Name.ToLowerInvariant()
    if (-not $assetsByName.ContainsKey($key)) {
        $assetsByName[$key] = New-Object System.Collections.ArrayList
    }
    [void]$assetsByName[$key].Add($asset)
}
 
function Resolve-Attachment {
    param(
        [string]$Target,
        [string]$NoteDirectory
    )
 
    $clean = Get-WikiTarget -RawTarget $Target
    if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($clean)) {
        return $null
    }
 
    if ($clean -match '^[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9+.-]*://') {
        return $null
    }
 
    $cleanFs = $clean -replace '/', '\'
 
    $sameFolder = Join-Path $NoteDirectory $cleanFs
    if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $sameFolder -PathType Leaf) {
        $item = Get-Item -LiteralPath $sameFolder
        if ($item.Extension -ine ".md") {
            return $item
        }
    }
 
    $fromRoot = Join-Path $VaultPath $cleanFs
    if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $fromRoot -PathType Leaf) {
        $item = Get-Item -LiteralPath $fromRoot
        if ($item.Extension -ine ".md") {
            return $item
        }
    }
 
    $leaf = Split-Path -Leaf $cleanFs
    if ($assetsByName.ContainsKey($leaf.ToLowerInvariant())) {
        $matches = @($assetsByName[$leaf.ToLowerInvariant()])
        if ($matches.Count -gt 1) {
            Write-Warning "Attachment '$clean' is ambiguous; using '$($matches[0].FullName)'."
        }
        return $matches[0]
    }
 
    return $null
}
 
$copiedAssets = @{}
 
foreach ($note in $publishedNotes) {
    $targets = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[string]
 
    foreach ($match in [regex]::Matches($note.Text, '\[\[([^\]]+)\]\]')) {
        $targets.Add($match.Groups[1].Value)
    }
 
    foreach ($match in [regex]::Matches($note.Text, '!?\[[^\]]*\]\(([^)]+)\)')) {
        $targets.Add($match.Groups[1].Value)
    }
 
    foreach ($target in $targets) {
        $asset = Resolve-Attachment -Target $target -NoteDirectory $note.Directory
        if (-not $asset) {
            continue
        }
 
        if ($copiedAssets.ContainsKey($asset.FullName)) {
            continue
        }
 
        $relativeAsset = Get-RelativePathFromRoot -Root $VaultPath -FullPath $asset.FullName
        $assetDestination = Join-Path $ContentRoot $relativeAsset
        $assetParent = Split-Path -Parent $assetDestination
 
        if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $assetParent)) {
            New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $assetParent -Force | Out-Null
        }
 
        Copy-Item -LiteralPath $asset.FullName -Destination $assetDestination -Force
        $copiedAssets[$asset.FullName] = $true
    }
}
 
Write-Host "Published notes: $($publishedNotes.Count)"
Write-Host "Referenced attachments copied: $($copiedAssets.Count)"
 
Write-Step "Building Quartz"
 
Push-Location -LiteralPath $QuartzRoot
try {
    if ($Serve) {
        Write-Host "Starting local preview at http://localhost:8080/"
        Write-Host "Press Ctrl+C when you're finished."
        & npx quartz build --serve
        exit $LASTEXITCODE
    }
 
    & npx quartz build
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {
        throw "Quartz build failed with exit code $LASTEXITCODE."
    }
}
finally {
    Pop-Location
}
 
Write-Step "Copying built website into the same Git repo"
 
$trackedParent = Split-Path -Parent $TrackedSiteRoot
if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $trackedParent)) {
    New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $trackedParent -Force | Out-Null
}
 
if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $TrackedSiteRoot)) {
    New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $TrackedSiteRoot -Force | Out-Null
}
 
& robocopy $PublicRoot $TrackedSiteRoot /MIR /R:2 /W:1 /NFL /NDL /NP
$robocopyExit = $LASTEXITCODE
 
if ($robocopyExit -ge 8) {
    throw "robocopy site staging failed with exit code $robocopyExit."
}
 
Write-Host "Tracked website output: $TrackedSiteRoot"
 
if (-not $SkipGit) {
    Write-Step "Backing up vault with Git"
 
    & git -C $VaultPath add -A
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {
        throw "git add failed."
    }
 
    $changes = & git -C $VaultPath status --porcelain
 
    if ($changes) {
        $commitMessage = "Publish Shag's Lab $(Get-Date -Format 'yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm')"
        & git -C $VaultPath commit -m $commitMessage
        if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {
            throw "git commit failed."
        }
    }
    else {
        Write-Host "Vault working tree is already clean."
    }
 
    $remotes = @(& git -C $VaultPath remote)
    if ($remotes -contains "origin") {
        & git -C $VaultPath push origin main
        if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {
            throw "git push failed."
        }
        Write-Host "Pushed vault backup to origin/main."
    }
    else {
        Write-Warning "No Git remote named 'origin' exists yet. Local Git backup is complete, but nothing was pushed off-machine."
    }
}
 
Write-Step "Done"
Write-Host "Quartz build output: $PublicRoot"
Write-Host "Tracked site output: $TrackedSiteRoot"
Write-Host ""
Write-Host "On the web host, run Update-ShagsLab-WebHost.bat."
Publish-ShagsLab-HomePC.bat
This is the button to press on the home PC.
@echo off
setlocal
 
rem === Shag's Lab publisher - HOME PC ===
rem Builds the public site from the Obsidian vault, copies the generated
rem site into the same Git repo under .site\public, then commits and pushes.
 
set "PUBLISHER=F:\[DIARY]\ShagsLab-Web\Publish-Lab.ps1"
 
echo.
echo ========================================
echo   Publishing Shag's Lab
echo ========================================
echo.
 
if not exist "%PUBLISHER%" (
    echo ERROR: Publisher script not found:
    echo   %PUBLISHER%
    echo.
    echo Make sure the one-repo Publish-Lab.ps1 is saved there.
    echo.
    pause
    exit /b 1
)
 
powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File "%PUBLISHER%"
 
if errorlevel 1 (
    echo.
    echo ========================================
    echo   PUBLISH FAILED
    echo ========================================
    echo.
    pause
    exit /b 1
)
 
echo.
echo ========================================
echo   Publish complete
echo ========================================
echo.
echo The vault, generated site, and Git history should now be pushed.
echo.
echo Next, on the WEB HOST, run:
echo   Update-ShagsLab-WebHost.bat
echo.
pause
 
exit /b 0
Update-ShagsLab-WebHost.bat
Save this somewhere convenient on the web host.
It pulls the private repository and mirrors only the generated site into Apache’s public folder.
@echo off
setlocal
 
rem === Shag's Lab website updater - WEB HOST ===
rem Pulls the latest repo from GitHub, then mirrors the generated site
rem into Apache's live web root.
 
set "REPO_DIR=C:\PGN\ShagsLab"
set "WEB_DIR=C:\xampp\htdocs\helvete\lab"
set "SITE_DIR=%REPO_DIR%\.site\public"
 
echo.
echo ========================================
echo   Updating Shag's Lab
echo ========================================
echo.
 
echo Checking Git...
where git >nul 2>&1
if errorlevel 1 (
    echo ERROR: Git is not installed or is not in PATH on this machine.
    echo.
    pause
    exit /b 1
)
 
git --version
echo.
 
if not exist "%REPO_DIR%\.git" (
    echo ERROR: Git repository not found:
    echo   %REPO_DIR%
    echo.
    echo The repo must be cloned to that folder first.
    echo.
    echo Example:
    echo   git clone YOUR_GITHUB_REPO_URL "%REPO_DIR%"
    echo.
    pause
    exit /b 1
)
 
cd /d "%REPO_DIR%"
 
echo Repository found.
echo.
echo Current remotes:
git remote -v
echo.
 
echo Pulling latest version from origin/main...
git pull --ff-only origin main
 
if errorlevel 1 (
    echo.
    echo ERROR: Git pull failed.
    echo Common causes:
    echo   - GitHub authentication is not set up on this PC
    echo   - origin is missing or points to the wrong repo
    echo   - the branch is not named main
    echo.
    pause
    exit /b 1
)
 
if not exist "%SITE_DIR%\index.html" (
    echo.
    echo ERROR: Generated site was not found:
    echo   %SITE_DIR%
    echo.
    echo Run Publish-ShagsLab-HomePC.bat on the home PC first,
    echo make sure it pushes successfully, then run this updater again.
    echo.
    pause
    exit /b 1
)
 
if not exist "%WEB_DIR%" (
    echo Creating live web folder:
    echo   %WEB_DIR%
    mkdir "%WEB_DIR%"
)
 
echo.
echo Publishing generated site to Apache...
robocopy "%SITE_DIR%" "%WEB_DIR%" /MIR /R:2 /W:1 /NFL /NDL /NP
 
if errorlevel 8 (
    echo.
    echo ERROR: Website copy failed.
    echo.
    pause
    exit /b 1
)
 
echo.
echo ========================================
echo   Shag's Lab is up to date
echo ========================================
echo.
echo Repository:
echo   %REPO_DIR%
echo.
echo Live website:
echo   %WEB_DIR%
echo.
pause
 
exit /b 0
Final sanity checklist
When everything is healthy:

F:\[DIARY]\Shag's Lab opens normally in Obsidian.
git status in the vault is clean after publishing.
The private GitHub repo has the newest commit.
.site\public\index.html exists in the repo.
C:\PGN\ShagsLab exists on the web host.
C:\xampp\htdocs\helvete\lab\index.html exists.
helvete.pizza/lab/ loads without a certificate warning.
win-acme shows healthy scheduled renewals.
Updates Home and Projects Home are being generated instead of maintained by hand.

If all of that is true:
Leave it alone.
It works.
Go make another weird thing.

projects/obsidian-vault-to-website/guide.content:
Shag’s Lab Metadata Standards
This is the house style for frontmatter in this vault. The goal is boring, predictable metadata so the publisher can do the clever stuff automatically.
Project Parents
Use project-parent for an umbrella/container that owns multiple child projects, not for every folder.
---
type: project-parent
project: Exact Parent Name
status: active
publish: true
---
Current project parents are Instruments, Keychron C100, and My Mini Retro Television.
Projects
---
type: project
project: Exact Project Name
status: active
publish: true
---
date, git, title, and project_aliases are optional. Do not keep an empty property as a placeholder.
Project Statuses

planned - defined, but work has not really started.
active - currently being worked on or actively maintained.
paused - intentionally on hold, with the expectation it may resume.
complete - the intended work is finished.
archived - retired, abandoned, or retained only for history.

For a project-parent, use active while at least one child project is active. A parent can become paused, complete, or archived when the collection as a whole reaches that state.
Updates
---
type: update
date: YYYY-MM-DD
project: Exact Project Name
publish: true
---
project may be omitted for a genuinely general update. For now, multi-project updates use a comma-separated list because the publisher already understands that format.
Guides
---
type: guide
project: Exact Project Name
publish: true
---
Guide statuses are separate from project lifecycle statuses. Use them only when useful:

living - actively maintained documentation.
snapshot - deliberately captures a point-in-time state.
complete - finished documentation that should not need routine updates.
deprecated - retained for history but no longer current.

Wiki
---
type: wiki
publish: true
---
Leave publish absent while an article is an empty/private draft.
Indexes
Folder landing pages use type: index. When a folder has a note named exactly Folder Name Home.md, the publisher can treat that note as the folder homepage.
Rules

Do not keep empty title, project, git, or youtube properties.
Use canonical project names consistently. Put old names in project_aliases on the Home note instead of continuing to use old names in new notes.
title is optional. Use it only when the display title should differ from the filename.
publish: true is an explicit public-site opt-in.
Keep filenames filesystem-safe; expressive punctuation belongs in title when needed.

projects/progeny-gaming-network/pgn-disc.content:
PGN Game Eras and Server Genealogy
This file separates three things that raw Discord statistics easily confuse:

a game was mentioned,
PGN was actively playing a game together,
PGN operated or seriously planned shared infrastructure for the game.

A Steam link is weak evidence of a clan era. Repeated direct invitations are stronger. A dedicated channel with hundreds of messages, server settings, and uptime problems is very strong.
The recurring families
MTA / GTA multiplayer
MTA → SAES/WSS/Helvete → FiveM → GT-MP → alt:V → FiveM zombie work → modern GTA-server discussions
This is PGN’s longest technical lineage. What persists is not one mod but a preferred shape of multiplayer: social open-world play, custom jobs, groups/gangs, scripting, server ownership, and the ability to make ridiculous systems the base game never intended.
The 2020 Hogwarts RP work demonstrates both the power and limitation of the lineage. PGN could build complex systems inside MTA, but the work remained tied to an aging mod and outside intellectual property. The Unity pivot later that year is therefore not a rejection of MTA; it is an attempt to carry the skills somewhere more durable.
Minecraft / Dargeath
Minecraft → Dargeath → lost backups → repeated nostalgia → vanilla returns → Dargeath 17.0
Minecraft is the purest shared-place game in PGN history.
Dargeath gives that pattern a named myth. Its loss turns it from old software into a lost world. Later Minecraft revivals repeatedly inherit the emotional goal even when they cannot inherit the original data.
Survival servers
ARK → 7 Days to Die → Grounded → Valheim → Palworld / Enshrouded / The Isle / ARK returns → Dune
These games generate the clearest communal eras because they create persistent places and maintenance obligations.
They also generate the most predictable PGN thought:

should we make a server?

Old-game resurrection
By 2026, resurrecting games nobody has touched in years is literally part of PGN’s own About-page description.
Battlefront II Classic is the culmination: an old game becomes the base for a modern database, website, progression system and Discord project.

Strong eras
Overwatch — late 2016 into 2018
The first major game visible after Discord begins. The archive explicitly refers to a Progeny Overwatch team and contains repeated invitations, season chatter and cosmetics.
ARK — January 2017
Server admin, RCON, updates, downtime and all-night taming make this a strong shared-world era.
PUBG — spring/summer 2017
One of the strongest invitation patterns in the early archive.
Factorio — July 2017
Short, concentrated and clearly multiplayer.
Fortnite — 2017–2018
PGN catches Fortnite before and after Battle Royale arrives.
Crossout — 2018 and 2023
A true recurring era. The later revival even becomes a recruiting funnel into PGN Discord roles.
7 Days to Die — May 2018
A compact server era followed almost immediately by interest in custom scripting.
MTA / SAES / Hogwarts — 2020
Heritage revival, active scripting, and a substantial custom server experiment.
Grounded — August 2022
Repeated organized sessions and shared-world excitement.
Valheim — 2022/2023, then major 2025 return
The idea survives across years before becoming a visible settlement/server era.
Helldivers II — March–May 2024
The strongest dedicated game thread of the modern archive.
Palworld — January–February 2024
A classic hot-and-fast shared-server phase.
The Isle — March 2025
Discord becomes field navigation: coordinates, player locations and server details.
Dune: Awakening — 2025 play, 2026 infrastructure
The later private-server work turns it into one of PGN’s technically richest hosting efforts.
Star Wars: Battlefront II Classic — 2026
The server is funny. The surrounding roadmap is historically significant.
PGN begins by running servers for games and gradually evolves toward building systems around games until the surrounding project is almost as large as the game itself.

projects/progeny-gaming-network/pgn-disc.content:
PGN Hall of Titles
Research Draft — Not Final Awards
The eventual titles should be funny because the people recognize the story, not because a script declared somebody’s personality.
Defensible metric-based candidates
The Ancient One
Tempa — authored the earliest surviving human message on 2016-10-19T16:33:46.954000-05:00.
The Chronicler
Shagwrath — largest surviving human text footprint at 15,616 messages.
Return From the Void
zZenom — longest observed text gap among members who later returned, about 2472 days.
The Pack Rat
Shagwrath — most attachment references, 2,126.
The Ping Lord
Shagwrath — most surviving @everyone uses, 149.
The Server Goblin
Shagwrath — most messages matching the transparent infrastructure vocabulary used in this report (server, host, script, code, api, repo, dedicated): 220.
New Blood, Ancient Volume
fart in a jar moosey — largest message footprint among people whose first archived text appears in 2022 or later, 3,210 messages.
Titles that need human judgment
Clan Troll
The original idea — somebody who has been around forever, contributed little in conventional terms, but supplied huge amounts of jokes, insults and trolling — is exactly the kind of title a machine should not decide alone.
A script can count swear words, joke markers, reactions and project links.
It cannot reliably distinguish affectionate insult from hostility, deadpan humor from seriousness, or contribution that happened entirely in voice chat.
The correct workflow is a shortlist plus clan argument.
Necromancer
Who most often revives dead games, servers or ideas?
Patron Saint of Bad Ideas
This needs stories, not counts.
The “One More Server” Award
Who is most responsible for the thought “should we make a server?”
Lorekeeper
Who remembers old players, old server details and forgotten events everybody else lost?
Professional Disappearing Act
Better nominated by the clan than inferred from text gaps.
Recommended process
Generate 3–5 candidates per title, post the evidence in Discord, let everyone argue, then preserve the winning explanation with the title.
The story is the award.
